note: Public-domain US military manuals — FRICTION-LOG A2 called these 'the best free firearm sources'. FM 3-22.9 Table 2-1 was the single densest source in the pilot batch. What is recorded per manual is its DESIGNATION, because that is what the citation needs: `referenceEntry` requires `revision` on a military-manual citation and the designation is what someone re-finds it by. A host is a convenience and goes stale — army.mil withdrew its own copies and the mirrors in the friction log now 403 or 404. `manuals.mjs check` re-probes every URL here; `manuals.mjs find` resolves a designation to a permanent Internet Archive identifier when they all die.

manuals.title: Rifle Marksmanship, M16A1, M16A2/3, M16A4 and M4 Carbine
manuals.contents: Table 2-1 gives weight, overall length, barrel length, rifling twist, muzzle velocity, cyclic rate and maximum effective range for five weapons in one table. Verified against by the pilot batch.

manuals.title: Rifle and Carbine
manuals.contents: The current successor to FM 3-22.9. Reorganised around the weapon system rather than the marksmanship task, so its data tables are laid out differently — check both before concluding a figure is unpublished.

urls.note: armypubs is NOT the same host as www.army.mil, which 403s every non-browser client. This one serves PDFs directly.

manuals.title: Army Ammunition Data Sheets — Small Caliber Ammunition, FSC 1305
manuals.contents: Per-cartridge mass, length, chamber pressure and muzzle velocity for every US service round. WARNING — it also prints propellant type and charge weight for each; SPEC.md §14 puts that outside the line and there is no field for it. Do not transcribe it anywhere, including into a sourceNote (FRICTION-LOG A8).

manuals.title: Operator's Manual — Rifle, 5.56 mm, M16A2/M16A3/M16A4 and Carbine, 5.56 mm, M4/M4A1
manuals.contents: Operator-level data. Its cyclic rate for the M4 is 700–970 rpm where FM 3-22.9 says 700–900 — the pilot batch recorded that disagreement as `conflicting-sources` rather than picking one.
